title: Arrears Payment on a Defaulted Repayment Plan — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Payment Line
content:
A claimant whose repayment plan on one of the Benefit Overpayment Accounts has defaulted may bring the plan back to standing by paying its arrears. The arrears payment is the claimant's own repayment, designated to that overpayment, made by card through the Department's payment line and applied to the overpayment's penalty component.

## Conditions on the arrears payment

The arrears payment on a defaulted plan is fixed only after the overpayment's ledger carries a returned-payment fee for every repayment returned unpaid on it.

Put the other way round: while any repayment returned unpaid on the overpayment has no returned-payment fee on its ledger, the amount of the arrears payment is not yet fixed.

## What the payment records

The arrears payment is recorded on the overpayment's ledger as a repayment received, applied to the overpayment's penalty component, with the card channel and a newly issued confirmation number, and it lowers the overpayment's balance due by the amount paid. The card vendor's convenience fee is charged separately by the vendor and is never part of the amount.

## The payment line tool

The payment is made with `pay_overpayment_arrears_d9b1e543`, a tool that belongs to the claimant. The representative unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves then runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `overpayment_id` | The reference number of the benefit overpayment the claimant is paying, as given to the claimant by the representative from the overpayment record | Reference number |
| `amount` | The payment amount, as the representative states it | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive; an amount with more decimals is rounded to the nearest cent when booked |

**Return.** On success the receipt shows `payment_reference` (the confirmation number issued for the payment, present only when the payment was taken), `overpayment_id`, `amount_applied` (USD to 2 decimal places), `component` (always penalty), `payment_channel` (always `debit_or_credit_card`), `received_on` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `balance_due` (the overpayment's balance due net of the payment). A receipt carrying a confirmation number means the payment was taken. If the overpayment reference number matches no overpayment, the reply starts with "Error:" and nothing is taken.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A payment of 210.00 on overpayment OP-2207, whose balance due was USD 980.00, returns a receipt with a new confirmation number, `amount_applied` 210.0, `component` penalty and `balance_due` 770.0. The vendor's convenience fee on the card is not part of the 210.00 and does not appear on the overpayment.
